meta.title: Euclide EBA — Authorised financial institutions in Europe

home.title: Is this institution really authorised in your country?
home.lead: Search a bank, a payment institution or an e-money institution and see, in plain language, its authorisation status, its supervisor and the official register where you can confirm it yourself.
home.searchPlaceholder: Bank name, BIC, city or country…
home.checkLead: Each country has one authority that grants and withdraws licences. Pick yours to see who supervises there and which institutions we list.
home.featuredLead: A sample of the largest supervised groups across the single market.
home.howTitle: How to protect yourself in three steps
home.how1Text: Marketing names differ from legal names. An authorisation is always granted to a legal entity.
home.how2Text: A payment or e-money licence is not a banking licence: your money is safeguarded differently and is not always covered by deposit guarantee.
home.how3Text: We always link to the supervisor’s own register. That register, not this site, is the legally binding source.

about.title: About Euclide EBA
about.lead: A public-interest reference for anyone who wants to know, in their own language, which financial institutions are authorised to operate in a given European country.
about.missionText: Authorisation registers exist in every European country, but they are scattered, technical and rarely translated. Euclide brings them together and explains them in seven languages, so that a citizen — in the EU or outside it — can check an institution before trusting it with their money.
about.dataText: Records are compiled from public supervisory sources: the EBA registers, the ECB list of supervised entities and the national registers linked on every page. Each institution page links back to the register of its own supervisor.
about.limitText: Euclide is an independent information service, not a supervisory authority. It gives no investment, legal or tax advice, and the entries here have no legal force. Before acting, always confirm the institution in the official register linked on its page.
about.langText: Financial exclusion often starts with language. The whole site — including institution descriptions — is available in English, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish and Arabic, with full right-to-left support.

footer.disclaimer: Independent information service. Not a supervisory authority and not affiliated with the institutions listed. The official register of the competent authority always prevails.
